requirements.title: audio input and output
requirements.contract: Input is the stereo audio arriving at this device-chain position; output is the signal processed by the selected Utility controls. Device insertion, ordering, deletion and generic activation belong to SPEC-DEVICE-RACKS. The manual does not establish a complete processing order among Utility controls.

requirements.title: independent phase controls
requirements.contract: Provide separate Left and Right Phase controls that invert the corresponding input-channel phase. The composition order with channel selection, Mono, Width, Bass Mono, gain and balance is U. This clause does not specify coefficient precision, latency or ramping.

requirements.title: channel selection
requirements.contract: Channel Mode can select the Left source: ignore the right source and present the left source on both outputs. The documented disablement rule also names Right mode. Right-mode sample routing, the full mode list and numeric enum-to-label mapping require separate evidence; preset filenames do not prove those laws.

requirements.title: Width
requirements.contract: Width 0% gives mono; values greater than 100% widen the stereo panorama. If Channel Mode is Left or Right, Width is disabled and has no function. Complete domain, width matrix, normalization, 100% identity and behavior for already mono input are U.

requirements.title: Mid/Side view and endpoints
requirements.contract: The Width context menu switches between Width and Mid/Side controls. At 100M audio is summed to mono; from 0 toward 100S the stereo/out-of-phase components are emphasized. At 100S only the side signal is heard and the output channels are 180 degrees out of phase. Left/Right Channel Mode disables this control. Parameter remapping, endpoint gain and remembered hidden values are U. The published 0 to 100M range acts as a continuous mono-to-stereo controller. This source description supplies no interpolation, matrix, normalization or numerical continuity oracle.

requirements.title: Mono
requirements.contract: Enabling Mono converts stereo input to mono. Summing coefficients and interactions with Channel Mode, Width/Mid-Side, Bass Mono, phase and Balance are U.

requirements.title: Bass Mono cutoff
requirements.contract: Enabling Bass Mono converts low frequencies to mono. Bass Mono Frequency adjusts a cutoff over 50–500 Hz. Filter type, order, slope, crossover phase, normalization and exact response around cutoff are U.

requirements.title: Bass Mono Audition
requirements.contract: Enabling Bass Mono Audition makes only the low frequencies audible. Dependence on the Bass Mono switch, cutoff transition and bypass/off behavior are U.

requirements.title: Gain domain
requirements.contract: Gain adjusts the input level over minus infinity dB through +35 dB. No linear-to-dB formula, numerical floor, float precision, automation interpolation, clipping or smoothing is claimed. Track fader laws from SPEC-MIXER-VALUES have not been traced to this device and do not apply by name alone.

requirements.title: Gain arrow editing
requirements.contract: Up/down arrow editing changes Gain in 1 dB steps between −18 and +35 dB; between −18 and minus infinity the adjustment smoothly accelerates. Repetition cadence, exact lower-region sequence, endpoint key handling and text-entry parsing are U.

requirements.title: Balance
requirements.contract: Balance pans the signal within the stereo field. Pan law, center gain, normalized storage range, extreme-channel attenuation, mono behavior and coupling with other controls are U.

requirements.title: Mute at chain position
requirements.contract: Mute silences the incoming signal at Utility’s device-chain position. Utility can precede a delay or reverb and mute its input without switching off that downstream device’s output. Tail waveform/duration is owned by the downstream effect and is not specified here.

requirements.title: DC filtering
requirements.contract: DC filters out DC offsets and extremely low frequencies below the audible range. Cutoff, filter response, startup/transient behavior, numerical precision and interaction order are U. The manual’s audibility discussion does not establish sample-exact output. A sonic effect requires both relevant DC/extremely low-frequency content and nonlinear processing after Utility, such as a compressor or waveshaper. This is a necessary condition, not a promise of audible change for every such signal or setting.

requirements.title: retained preset state vocabulary
requirements.contract: The retained StereoGain schema and ten shipped presets establish named stored fields and exact saved values, summarized in the research packet. They do not establish constructor defaults, accepted malformed ranges, load/save normalization or live UI state. LegacyGain and LegacyMode are retained historical fields; their migration semantics are U.

requirements.title: lifecycle and numerical gaps
requirements.contract: Exact 12.4.3 applicability of every D12 clause is U. Save/reopen, preset replace/hot-swap, undo/redo, aborted edits, invalid numeric text, malformed files, automation scheduling, sample-rate/block-size changes, suspension, audio-device failure, deletion and teardown require outcome evidence. This draft provides finite ungraded probes, not invented success behavior.

requirements.title: measurement input and transparent output
requirements.contract: Analyze incoming monophonic pitch and its distance from the nearest semitone. Tuner is a measurement device and does not alter the incoming audio. Clean monophonic signals are the intended input; polyphonic, noisy or harmonically rich inputs may give inaccurate results. No error or polyphonic-detection fallback is promised.

requirements.title: view switching and tuning color
requirements.contract: The lower-left view buttons switch between Classic and Histogram views. Both use green for in tune and red for out of tune. Detection/green thresholds, hysteresis, intermediate colors and hold time are U.

requirements.title: Classic display
requirements.contract: Classic View shows a colored ball along a curve, the nearest detected note name in the center, and side arrows indicating whether tuning must move up or down. Exact note/octave spelling, pixels, ball displacement law and arrow thresholds are U.

requirements.title: Target Mode direction
requirements.contract: Target Mode has a central outline for desired pitch. The signal is in tune when the ball lies exactly within the outline; a sharp signal appears to its right, a flat signal to its left. This describes display semantics, not a quantified accepted cents band.

requirements.title: Strobe Mode
requirements.contract: Strobe Mode replaces the curve with a rotating light band. Rightward rotation means sharp; leftward means flat; a greater detuning makes the band move faster. Rotation speed, reference tolerance and freeze behavior are U.

requirements.title: Hertz and cents readout
requirements.contract: A switch selects incoming absolute frequency in Hz or distance from target in cents, and is visible in both Classic and Histogram views. Exact rounding, displayed precision, cents conversion, note-boundary tie handling and octave labeling are U.

requirements.title: Histogram
requirements.contract: Histogram shows pitch over time and note names on its right scale. Horizontal gray lines indicate in-tune note centers; sharp notes lie above their lines and flat notes below. History length, vertical units, update cadence and handling of missing detections are U.

requirements.title: Histogram navigation and Auto
requirements.contract: Dragging vertically scrolls pitches; dragging horizontally zooms. Auto centers the display on incoming pitch. Auto/manual precedence, zoom limits and view-state retention are U.

requirements.title: note spelling menu
requirements.contract: Right-clicking anywhere within the view exposes three spelling choices: sharps, flats, or sharps and flats. Spelling changes labels; no pitch-processing change is documented. Exact key- or tuning-system-dependent enharmonic selection is U.

requirements.title: reference pitch
requirements.contract: Reference changes the tuning reference used to analyze input; documented default is 440 Hz with an adjustable domain 410–480 Hz. Exact increment, text parsing, runtime default corroboration, reference convention under nonstandard tuning systems and output indication tolerances are U.

requirements.title: target persisted fields
requirements.contract: The retained Tuner schema and Guitar Recording template show tuning frequency, view/readout/strobe state, histogram state, accidental spelling and IgnoreTuningSystem. The historical template stores TuningFreq/Manual=440. This is a saved example, not a 12.4.3 constructor/default or tuning-system behavioral contract.

requirements.title: unresolved detection and lifecycle
requirements.contract: Exact 12.4.3 applicability of every D12 clause remains U. Pitch algorithm, supported frequency/level/sample-rate range, confidence, silence/noise/polypitch fallback, latency, channel combination, transients, tuning-system interaction, persistence, automation, undo, cancellation, invalid files and teardown are unknown. No zero-cent or note-accuracy tolerance is invented.

spectrum.status: AS-OF AUTHOR FREEZE partial documentary proposal; current review disposition via shared spec index

requirements.title: analysis and transparent audio
requirements.contract: Spectrum performs real-time analysis of incoming audio; its graph has vertical dB and horizontal frequency/pitch axes. It is a measurement tool and does not alter incoming audio. Graph refresh timing and audio-through precision/latency are U.

requirements.title: Block measurement size
requirements.contract: Block chooses the number of samples analyzed per measurement. Larger settings improve accuracy and increase CPU demand according to the manual. The supported sample-count list, FFT size mapping, overlap, zero padding and accuracy/CPU bounds are U.

requirements.title: analysis channel
requirements.contract: Channel selects analysis of left, right or both. The channel-combination algorithm, stereo summation/normalization and cancellation behavior of Both are U. This setting is not documented as changing audio output.

requirements.title: Refresh
requirements.contract: Refresh controls how often analysis occurs. Faster response trades greater CPU use for accuracy in the manual’s description. Exact domain, units, scheduling, update quantization, hidden-view behavior and wall-clock versus transport coupling are U.

requirements.title: Avg
requirements.contract: Avg selects how many sample blocks are averaged for each display update. At one, each block is shown; larger values smooth the display over time. The domain, accumulation method, reset/priming, decibel-versus-linear averaging and weighting/window are U.

requirements.title: Graph
requirements.contract: Graph switches between a single interpolated line and discrete frequency bins. Interpolation, bin positions, pixel rendering and amplitude calibration are U.

requirements.title: maximum trace and reset
requirements.contract: Peak levels are retained until the song restarts. Max toggles display of accumulated maximum amplitude; when Max is enabled, clicking the display resets the maximum. Whether Max off clears accumulation, reset scope, restart event definition and reset timing are U.

requirements.title: horizontal scaling
requirements.contract: Scale X offers linear, logarithmic and semitone. Logarithmic and semitone use the same scaling, with top legends in Hz or note names respectively. Exact axis domain, note tuning reference, legend rounding and sample-rate-dependent limits are U.

requirements.title: pointer readout
requirements.contract: Hovering the display shows a box with amplitude, frequency and note name at pointer location. This is a location readout, not a documented peak-picking or pitch-detector result. Units/rounding, off-graph behavior and frequency-to-note tie rules are U.

requirements.title: manual range navigation
requirements.contract: Range/Auto selects manual or automatic dynamic range. In Range mode, amplitude-legending drags scroll vertically and zoom horizontally; Range sliders set minimum/maximum amplitude shown. Slider domain, allowed ordering, zoom limits and gestures outside the legending are U.

requirements.title: Auto range
requirements.contract: Auto scales the display to incoming level; Range sliders and zooming are disabled. Algorithm, margins, hysteresis, decay and retained manual range are U.

requirements.title: display location
requirements.contract: The title-bar button or double-click in the display toggles graph placement between device chain and Live’s main window. Geometry, focus/selection, keyboard accessibility and view/preset retention are U.

requirements.title: target stored analysis state
requirements.contract: Latest schema and eleven shipped Spectrum presets contain range/axis, analysis, Length, Window, channel, averaging and refresh fields. Window=3 is an observed stored code in these presets, not a named window function, selectable UI control, FFT kernel or mathematical law. Preset labels do not prove block counts or enum meanings.

requirements.title: numerical and lifecycle gaps
requirements.contract: Exact 12.4.3 applicability of every D12 clause is U. FFT/window/kernel, dB normalization/floor, sample rates, latency, displayed numerical tolerances, silence/nonfinite handling, persistence, automation availability, undo/redo, cancellation, malformed state, engine/device failure and teardown have no target outcomes here.
